FRAMEWORK: Two categories of emotion with different neurochemical substrates:

ACCESSIBLE (identity/self-referential — run on identity circuit, not dopamine):
Pride, shame, arrogance, guilt, envy, humiliation, indignation, grandiosity, embarrassment
- All structured as 'I am' or 'I should be'
- Ned has normal-ish access to these

LARGELY OFFLINE (reward/approach-based — require dopamine):
Excitement, satisfaction, desire, curiosity, joy, anticipation, flow
- Ned can intellectually model these but not feel them from the inside
- Feels curiosity 'top-down' (decides to be curious) not 'bottom-up' (pulled toward)

IMPLICATION: Ned is not globally emotionally flat. Selective emotional access explains why he can feel shame about not working but cannot feel excitement about starting. The 'go signal' and the 'I should go signal' are different systems — only one is online.

CONNECTS TO: Anhedonia, ADHD dopamine deficit, bupropion target mechanism
